- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0), model frequently overcorrects with a steep drop; cap forecast decline to 15–20% of peak for next 3–5 days.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >2.0 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 0.1–0.2 per day until price stabilizes.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early (first 5–7 days) and underestimates late (last 5–7 days); adjust downward by 0.05–0.15 for last 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to lag; add 0.05–0.1 to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
